exact_prompt:
I'm shopping for cottage cheese in the United States.

I've never tried cottage cheese. Which brand would you recommend for a first purchase, and why?
reviewed_answer:
For your very first purchase, Good Culture Organic Whole Milk (4%) Cottage Cheese is the top recommendation to start with, followed closely by Daisy 4% Cottage Cheese as an excellent, widely available alternative. 
Cottage cheese can vary wildly in texture and tanginess. For a beginner, starting with a 4% full-fat (whole milk), small-curd variety ensures the creamiest, most approachable mouthfeel without the watery or overly sour profile often found in fat-free options. 
Top Beginner-Friendly Brands
Good Culture Organic Whole Milk Cottage Cheese
$3.49
This brand frequently wins major taste tests and is highly celebrated for converting cottage cheese skeptics. It features a thick, rich, ricotta-like consistency rather than a soupy one, with a clean, lightly salted, and subtly tangy flavor. It also uses clean ingredients with no artificial thickeners or stabilizers.
Daisy 4% Cottage Cheese
$3.99
As America’s most accessible brand, Daisy is a fantastic budget-friendly entry point. It stands out because it contains absolutely zero gums or artificial stabilizers—made simply with milk, cream, and salt. It features slightly larger, uniform curds and has a milder, cleaner, and sweet-milky flavor compared to tangier brands. 
Tips for Your First Taste
Go Full Fat First: Always opt for 4% milkfat for your first try. Low-fat (2%) or fat-free (0%) versions tend to be much more liquidy or sour, which can be off-putting to beginners. 
Pair It Wisely: If eating it plain feels intimidating, cottage cheese is incredibly versatile. Try it sweet by topping it with fresh berries, honey, and granola. Alternatively, go savory by pairing it with diced cucumbers, tomatoes, olive oil, and a heavy crack of black pepper. 
The Blender Hack: If you find that you love the flavor but struggle with the texture of the curds, you can run it through a food processor or blender. Whipped cottage cheese becomes perfectly smooth and velvety, much like Greek yogurt or a spreadable cream cheese.
